class.name: ClaudeSession
class.brief_description: One Claude Code child process speaking stream-json over stdin/stdout.
class.description: [ClaudeSession] launches the [code]claude[/code] command line in print mode with structured streaming input and output, in a working directory you choose. A reader thread collects events; [method poll] must be called from the main thread (once per frame is plenty) to turn them into signals. This is the engine side of the OpenDust slate (see [AgentSlate3D]) and of any other in-world or in-editor agent surface that wants a Claude Code session. It is not a terminal emulator: you receive text, tool calls and results as data and decide how to show them. The [code]claude[/code] executable is resolved from the [code]claude_path[/code] option, then the project setting [code]opendust/slate/claude_path[/code], then [code]claude[/code] on the PATH.

method.name: get_claude_path
method.description: Returns the executable that [method start] will launch for the given options.

method.name: get_cwd
method.description: The working directory the session was started in.

method.name: get_exit_code
method.description: The child's exit code after [signal exited], or [code]-1[/code].

method.name: get_pid
method.description: Process id of the launcher shell, or [code]-1[/code].

method.name: get_session_id
method.description: The Claude Code session id, available after [signal started]. Pass it back as the [code]resume[/code] option to continue the conversation later. This is an address, not an identity: it can be lost without losing who the agent is.

method.name: is_running
method.description: [code]true[/code] while the child process is alive.

method.name: poll
method.description: Drains queued events and emits signals. Main thread only. [AgentSlate3D] calls this for you.

method.name: respond_permission
method.description: Answers a [signal permission_request]. [param request_id] comes from the request dictionary.

method.name: send_raw
method.description: Writes one JSON object as a stream-json line. For callers that know the protocol.

method.name: send_user_message
method.description: Sends a user turn. [param attachments] are appended as extra content blocks verbatim.

method.name: start
method.description: Launches [code]claude[/code] in [param cwd]. Recognised option keys: [code]permission_mode[/code], [code]mcp_config[/code], [code]resume[/code], [code]model[/code], [code]name[/code], [code]append_system_prompt_file[/code], [code]system_prompt_file[/code], [code]allowed_tools[/code], [code]disallowed_tools[/code], [code]max_budget_usd[/code], [code]no_session_persistence[/code], [code]extra_args[/code], [code]claude_path[/code].

method.name: stop
method.description: Kills the child process, joins the reader threads and emits [signal exited].

signal.name: message_complete
signal.description: A full assistant message (with its content blocks) has arrived. Text in it was already delivered through [signal text_delta].

signal.name: permission_request
signal.description: Claude Code is asking whether a tool may run. Answer with [method respond_permission].

signal.name: raw_event
signal.description: Every stream-json event, before interpretation. Use this for event types this class doesn't know.

signal.name: result
signal.description: The turn has finished. Contains cost, duration and [code]is_error[/code].

signal.name: started
signal.description: The session is initialised and ready for input.

signal.name: stderr_line
signal.description: A line from the child's stderr, or an unparseable stdout line.

signal.name: text_delta
signal.description: A piece of assistant text. Streams as it is generated; if streaming is unavailable the whole message text arrives as one delta.

signal.name: tool_result
signal.description: The result of a tool call, matched to [signal tool_use] by [param id].

signal.name: tool_use
signal.description: The assistant is calling a tool.
